strengths: Addresses an important and novel problem combining interactive 4D scene expansion with consistent environmental dynamics generation, filling a meaningful gap between static 3D generation and uncontrolled 4D video synthesis

Well-designed technical pipeline that thoughtfully combines multiple components: Eulerian flow for environmental dynamics, geometry-aware alignment for resolving view ambiguities, hash-based neural motion field for continuous queries, and bidirectional motion propagation for coverage

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across visual quality, motion consistency, and physical plausibility metrics, with extensive ablation studies validating each design choice and demonstrating the contribution of key components

Achieves competitive or superior empirical results across multiple benchmarks, particularly strong on motion quality and temporal consistency while maintaining practical real-time interactivity (~12 seconds including rendering)

Demonstrates practical interactive system capability with user studies showing preference over baselines and positive interactivity ratings, supported by well-documented supplementary material with implementation details
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty in individual components: Eulerian flow estimation, Kabach algorithm, and multi-resolution hash encoding are all established techniques; the main novel contribution (geometry-aware alignment) is a relatively straightforward combination of existing methods

Evaluation lacks direct comparison with comparable interactive 4D expansion methods; video generation baselines are not designed for controllable camera motion and interactive expansion, making these comparisons somewhat unfair and limiting assessment of the true technical contribution

Insufficient analysis of method limitations: rigid body motion is acknowledged as out-of-scope but no systematic evaluation of impact; hash-based motion field designed for environmental dynamics lacks analysis of generalization to other motion types; no failure case documentation

Reproducibility concerns including no mention of code/dataset release, incomplete training specification for motion field, and critical implementation details scattered across supplementary sections requiring integration for implementation

User studies are modest in scale (95 for 2AFC, 20 for interactivity study with specialized backgrounds) and lack analysis of sensitivity to motion inconsistencies or coverage of diverse environmental dynamics types

strengths: Novel problem formulation addressing an underexplored task of interactive 4D world generation with environmental dynamics from single images
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including quantitative metrics (VBench, PhysReal), human preference studies (95 participants, 2AFC), ablation studies, and extensive qualitative results
Solid technical execution combining Eulerian flow, geometry-aware alignment via Kabsch algorithm, and hash-based neural motion field in a principled manner
Demonstrates genuine interactivity with practical system achieving ~12 seconds for initial generation and ~3 seconds for updates with live visual feedback
Well-organized presentation with clear methodology, thorough supplementary material, and detailed implementation specifications aiding reproducibility
Thoughtful approach to handling boundary issues through bidirectional motion propagation with opacity scheduling
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty with individual components being well-established (Eulerian flow from optical flow literature, hash encoding from Instant-NGP, Kabsch algorithm), making contributions primarily engineering-focused rather than methodologically innovative

Problematic baseline comparisons—video generation models (Veo 3.1, CogVideoX, Tora) were not designed for 4D geometric consistency, and 4D baselines (4DGS-Cinemagraphy, PerpetualWonder) target different offline scenarios, making performance claims difficult to evaluate. Only modest human preference (~60-65%) despite being the only direct baseline

Severely limited scope of environmental dynamics restricted to clouds, water, smoke/fog, and fire—all relatively simple particle/fluid phenomena. No complex object interactions, rigid body dynamics, or multi-body systems, significantly limiting generality and applicability

Evaluation limitations inherent to single-image generation task: no ground truth possible, non-reference metrics are subjective, PhysReal metric evaluates rendered geometry plausibility rather than actual dynamics accuracy. Cannot verify if generated dynamics match physical reality

Geometric consistency concerns despite claims of 'globally coherent' dynamics—still relies on reprojection-based correspondence susceptible to failure in complex occlusions (Fig. 3). Minimal analysis of failure cases in qualitative results with visible artifacts in newly revealed areas

Ad-hoc design choices lacking thorough justification: opacity scheduler formulation (Eqs. 11-12) appears heuristic without principled basis, specific hash encoding parameters lack ablation studies, gradient-based refinement is standard but not analyzed in depth
Borderline interactivity claim: 12 seconds for scene generation is not truly real-time despite being called 'interactive,' representing batch-processing speed rather than interactive generation

Insufficient ablation studies: Table 3 lacks detailed explanation of why geometry-aware alignment outperforms alternatives, no ablation on opacity scheduler design, limited analysis of hash field design choices
Reproducibility concerns including no code release mention, hyperparameter tuning details not fully documented, and some design choices appearing dataset-specific that may not generalize

Limited comparative analysis: no comparison with recent text-to-4D methods, missing discussion of fundamental differences from traditional 4D reconstruction methods, relatively small 60-scene benchmark

strengths: Addresses an important and well-motivated problem in interactive 4D scene generation—maintaining globally coherent environmental dynamics during scene expansion, which existing methods largely ignore
Clever geometry-aware alignment module that effectively resolves directional and scale ambiguities in 3D space using spatial correspondences and gradient-based refinement

Comprehensive evaluation with multiple complementary metrics (VBench for visual/temporal quality, PhysReal for physical plausibility), diverse baselines across video generation and 4D methods, and human study with 95 participants showing consistent preference for LivingWorld

Hash-based motion field with bidirectional propagation is an efficient and practical representation enabling continuous motion queries without per-Gaussian optimization, with careful design choices (opacity scheduler, boundary hole analysis) addressing technical challenges

Achieves practical interactivity (~12 seconds per expansion) suitable for real-time user feedback, with detailed implementation details supporting reproducibility and an interactive interface supporting user guidance

Excellent presentation with effective visualizations demonstrating coherent dynamics across diverse environmental scenarios, clear algorithmic descriptions, and thorough supplementary material with extensive ablation studies
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—individual components (Eulerian flow, Gaussian splatting, hash encodings) are well-established techniques; primary novelty is the geometry-aware alignment module, which while effective, is somewhat incremental (Kabsch algorithm applied to scene-flow samples with gradient refinement)

Constrained scope limited to fluid-like environmental dynamics (clouds, water, smoke, fire); acknowledged inability to handle articulated motion, rigid-body dynamics, or physics-constrained motion significantly limits generality and impact for broad 4D scene generation

Evaluation limitations: only 60 scenes in main benchmark is modest for establishing robust generalization; baseline comparisons somewhat unfair since video generation models aren't designed for 3D consistency and 4D scene methods aren't designed for controllable environmental dynamics; missing physics-informed dynamics comparisons

Computational cost limits true interactivity—12 seconds per expansion step prevents rapid exploration; requires high-end hardware (RTX 6000); motion field training dominates runtime (Table 5) with limited analysis of scaling properties

Motion field design choices lack principled justification: linear velocity field assumption may break down for complex rotational or non-rigid dynamics; Lagrangian vs. Eulerian choice is pragmatic but not theoretically motivated; very limited failure case analysis beyond Figure 15

User study only provides win rates through 2AFC comparisons without explaining why LivingWorld is preferred; interactivity evaluation (D.7) separated from perceptual study; unclear how additional controls affect combined user experience; limited statistical significance testing

Generalization concerns inadequately addressed: training on curated datasets (Pexels, Unsplash) with unclear performance on arbitrary or unconstrained images; no domain shift analysis; learned motion field vocabulary limited to training scenarios

Missing design analysis: no ablation on hash grid resolution, MLP architecture, or sensitivity to hyperparameters (e.g., why 300 iterations for alignment refinement?); limited theoretical grounding for specific architectural choices
